data.description:
## Problem

Calibration 4 (the first code-v5 segmented replay; the thresholds in force were adjudicated on
the code-v3 corpus, and ADR 0036 forbids pooling across impact-model versions) adjudicated the
findings each proposed flip would newly block, by reading them rather than by validity proxy.
Two criteria are cleared to move.

## Scope

Exactly two edits to `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json`:

1. `security`: `block_threshold` 0.54 -> 0.45 (stays `blocking_enabled: true`).
2. `concurrency`: `default_posture` advisory -> blocking, `block_threshold` 0.95 -> 0.52,
   `blocking_enabled` false -> true.

Each edit carries an inline `_comment` naming this ticket and its evidence, matching the
convention already used by the `api-compat` and `tests` entries.

## Evidence

- `security` @0.45: 13 newly-blocking findings, adjudicated 13 TP-blockworthy, 0 nit, 0 FP.
  Friction 0.29% -> 1.43% of changes (10 of 701). Mean validity of the would-block set 0.990,
  zero findings below validity 0.5. Every one names a hole in a guard that already exists.
- `concurrency` @0.52: 2 newly-blocking, both TP-blockworthy, 0 nit, 0 FP. Friction 0.29%.
  It was held advisory at the prior calibration solely because n=1 was below the script's
  MIN_N=25 power floor; the code-v5 segment gives it n=68 (53 surviving), so the hold reason
  has expired. 0.52 rather than 0.50: the three adjudicated nits all sit at priority 0.5143
  and 0.52 excludes them, and it limits the `threshold_for` MIN-rule leak onto co-tagged
  `correctness` findings to 0.02.

## Non-goals

- `maintainability` routing (53% nit+FP at the measured threshold; deferred).
- Any change to `impact_code`. A `blast_radius`/`debt_impact` severity floor was measured and
  REJECTED: 44% of the 48 findings it would newly block were nits or FPs.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` has `security.block_threshold == 0.45`
      and `security.blocking_enabled == true`.
      Oracle: `python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json'));assert d['security']['block_threshold']==0.45 and d['security']['blocking_enabled'] is True"`
      exits 0.
- [ ] The same file has `concurrency.block_threshold == 0.52`,
      `concurrency.blocking_enabled == true`, `concurrency.default_posture == "blocking"`.
      Oracle: `python -c "import json;d=json.load(open('src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json'));c=d['concurrency'];assert c['block_threshold']==0.52 and c['blocking_enabled'] is True and c['default_posture']=='blocking'"`
      exits 0.
- [ ] Both entries carry an `_comment` citing this ticket id.
      Oracle: `grep -c "<this ticket id>" src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` returns >= 2.
- [ ] No other criterion's posture or threshold changes.
      Oracle: `git diff src/rebar/llm/code_review/criteria_routing.json` touches only the
      `security` and `concurrency` objects.
- [ ] `make verify` is green.
- [ ] The Gerrit change is MERGED (LLM-Review +1, Verified +1).
data.title: Route security at 0.45 and concurrency blocking at 0.52 from the code-v5 calibration
